chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Buraiz al-Razzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

O my son, know that the rank of the Shi'a is based upon the degree of their narrating and conscious knowledge, for indeed, conscious knowledge is comprehension of the narration. With comprehensions of the narrations, the believer elevates to the farthest levels of faith. Indeed, I have looked into the book of Ali (peace be upon him) and I found in the book: Indeed, the value and rank of every person is his conscious knowledge. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will judge people in accordance to the amount of what He has granted them of intellects in the life of this world.
ai.seo_question: How is the spiritual rank of a believer determined according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the intrinsic link between *al-darayah* (deep comprehension) and *al-riwayah* (narration transmission), establishing that spiritual rank is proportional to one's grasp of hadith. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on intellectual rigor, where divine judgment is calibrated to the intellect (*aql*) bestowed upon each individual, reflecting the principle that accountability matches capacity.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from Muhammed bin ‘Isa, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Zaid al-Razzaz, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, said:

O my son, know that the rank of the Shi’a [1] is based upon the degree of their narrating and conscious knowledge, for indeed, conscious knowledge is comprehension. With comprehensions of the narrations, the believer elevates to the farthest levels of faith. Indeed, I have looked into the book of Ali, peace be upon him, and I found in the book: Indeed, the value and rank of every person is his conscious knowledge. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will judge people in accordance to the amount of what He has granted them of intellects in the life of this world.
